questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Republic of the Congo?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Republic of the Congo article.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Brazzaville?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Republic of the Congo is Brazzaville.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Republic of the Congo?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Republic of the Congo on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Republic of the Congo article.

questions.proof: It is also bordered by Gabon to the west, Cameroon and the Central African Republic to the north, and Cabinda (Angola) to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Republic of the Congo about 342,000 square kilometres; Malawi about 118,484 square kilometres; Eritrea about 117,600 square kilometres; Benin about 114,763 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Republic of the Congo in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Republic of the Congo on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Republic of the Congo on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.proof: Republic of the Congo is in Africa.
